_readme: The Xeno Warriors Guide (guide book item + the Guide tab in the main menu). When you add or change a feature, add or update its page here. Text: '\n' for new lines, lines starting '- ' are bullets, '## ' a sub-heading. {key:NAME} shows the player's key for key.xenowarriors.NAME. A chapter or page with "requires": "<modid>" only shows when that mod is installed; "season": N only once Season N is unlocked.

pages.title: Welcome, warrior
pages.text:
You play as a character from Xeno Warriors Recarnet, each with their own skills, ultimate, fighting style, outfits and stats.
## Choosing a character
- The first time you join you pick a warrior. Switch any time: main menu > Character Select, or /xeno choose.
- Each character keeps their own levels, loadout, inventory, faction standing and ability levels.
- Switching ends the old character's stances and takeovers (Boxing Stance, Persephone, Zane's Projection, Hekublade Scatter blades still in the air...). Potion effects from skills stay.
- Season 2 and 3 characters and content stay locked until an operator runs /xeno season unlock 2 (or 3), so nothing spoils the show. /xeno season lock locks them again: a Season 2/3 character can't use skills, its ultimate or KA, and Season 2/3 outfits come off.

pages.title: Keys
Karma
pages.text:
Karma is the energy every skill runs on (Zane calls his mana, Ultima his Data, but it's the same bar).
- Every skill costs Karma on top of its cooldown.
- It refills slowly by itself, much faster while you crouch and stand still to focus, fully after a night's sleep, and with Karma Potions.
- Karma Sensing ({key:karma_sense}) lets you feel every living thing's Karma nearby: they glow through walls for a few seconds, each inside an aura you can see through walls too. Range and time grow with practice. A Karma-reducing hoodie hides you from it.
- The aura's size shows how strong something is next to you: weaker things give off a modest glow, your equals a tall one, and anything far stronger than you - and every boss - a giant blazing column (up to about 7 blocks wide and 15-20 tall) that burns white-hot in the middle. Strength counts its level, health, attack and armor (and DragonMineZ power, if installed).

pages.title: The main menu
pages.text:
Press {key:stats_menu} for the main menu:
- Character Select and Character Customization (stats, skill loadout and ability tiers, outfits, KA / last resort)
- Party (your team, bots, synergy and bond)
- Pets, Factions, Journey, Warriors (everyone online), Settings (cel-shading, HUD style, Karma Sensing, movement, combat)
- Guide: this book.

pages.title: Combos and heavy hits
pages.text:
What you hold decides your combo, for players and bots alike.
- Left click to chain hits. Clicking early only queues the next one, so timing beats spamming.
- The last hit of a string is a finisher that knocks enemies away.
- Sneak + left click: a slow heavy hit that launches and breaks shields.
- A perfectly chained string is a little stronger than plain vanilla hits with the same weapon.

pages.title: Guns and dashing in
pages.text:
## Guns
- Holding a gun (TACZ guns, or any gun from this mod) your clicks never start a combo string: you stand still and shoot, the gun's own aim and fire (left click fires, hold right click to aim down the sights - Mikiko's and Rhalix's summoned guns too).
## Dashing in
- Mikiko's and Rhalix's combos only dash or step forward when the hit will land: someone you're aiming at, locked on to, or right in front of you, close enough to reach.
- Swinging at the air (or at someone too far off) you stay where you are - no dashing around. Rhalix's Kishi Warp (hold attack while running) still goes the distance.

pages.title: Skills and ultimates
pages.text:
- Every character has 4 skill slots and an ultimate. Pick them in Character Customization > Skills: click a slot, then a skill card.
- More skills (and sometimes other ultimates) unlock at higher Character Levels.
- Skills level up as you use them, with tier upgrades: see Progression > Ability levels and tiers.
- Mikiko and Rhalix's last resort is the Xeno Blast ({key:super_ultimate_ctrl6}): a short charge, then a huge blast that pours out ALL your Karma (at least 10). The more Karma, the harder it hits - and your Karma won't come back for 30 seconds.
## Hit during a cutscene
- Enemy hits during your ultimate, team ultimate or Xeno Blast cutscene land (no knockback), but your Guard holds: it takes 3 hits that count to break it. Then the cutscene ends and you get your camera and controls back to defend yourself. A GUARD x/3 meter shows each hit.
- Defense makes hits less likely to count: every hit counts at Defense 0, about 3 in 4 at Defense 50, 57% at 200, 35% at 1,000 and 20% (the lowest) from 3,000 up. Shrugged-off hits show RESISTED with a shield clang.
- Big damage always breaks it, whatever your Defense: one hit of 20% or more of your max health, or 35% of your max health taken over the cutscene (with DragonMineZ, its damage and max health).
- Gravity Barrage and the Gravity Fox Fire team ultimate: the rest of the attack lands on its targets all at once. Blazing Wind: the tornado carries on by itself. Xeno Blast: you're free to move and the blast still fires at its normal moment. Nothing is refunded.
- Beam clashes are never cut short.
## Charging your ultimate
- The ultimate key charges your ultimate first (1.5 seconds), then it goes off. Hold the key to keep charging - up to 5 seconds, for up to +50% power - and let go to unleash it.
- While you charge, a teammate who can do a team ultimate with you (Mikiko + Rhalix) joins by pressing their own ultimate key, and it becomes the team ultimate.
- A bot teammate who can team up joins once you've held the key for 2 seconds (just tap it for your own ultimate).
- Sneak + ultimate still asks your partner for a team ultimate straight away.

pages.title: KAs
pages.text:
A KA is a character's super ultimate ({key:super_ultimate_ctrl6}) - Kaeru's Change, Max's Vampire Cut, Logan's Redirect, Zane's Projection, Keita's KA and more.
- Every KA has a price that gets worse the more you use it; too many uses close together burn it out for a while.
- Character Customization > KAs shows yours, and the KA & Element Guide explains every one.

pages.title: Clashes
pages.text:
Fire a blast skill at an enemy charging their own blast at you (or two players fire at each other within half a second) and the blasts lock together between you.
- Mash left click to push. NPCs push with their Karma.
- Whoever gets pushed back eats both blasts.
- With DragonMineZ, your blasts can clash with ki attacks too.

pages.title: Lock-on
pages.text: Press {key:lock_on} to lock onto whatever is closest to your crosshair: your view stays turned to it, a reticle spins on it and its health shows at the top of the screen. Press again to let go; it also lets go if the target dies, gets too far or stays out of sight. Some moves (Mikiko's rope blade throw) home in on your lock-on target.

pages.title: Team attacks
pages.text:
## Team ultimates
Mikiko and Rhalix on the same side (party members, you and your bot, or two bots), within 12 blocks:
- One of them sneaks and presses the ultimate key ({key:ultimate_ctrl5}).
- The other gets a request: press the ultimate key (or {key:accept_request}, or click [Join]) to join. A bot partner joins straight away if it's ready.
- Still waiting? Sneak + ultimate again to switch to the other team ultimate (it remembers your pick).
- It uses both ultimates' cooldowns and 40 Karma from both. If enemy hits break your Guard mid-cutscene (see Combat > Skills and ultimates), the rest of it lands at once. Bot partners can't be hit during it.
## Gravity Fox Fire
Rhalix slams down a Kishi dome that pins the enemies, then Mikiko's fox fire storms through it, ending in one big blast.
## Blazing Judgment
Once Rhalix knows Judgment Absorption (Character Level 30): his gravity point drags every enemy around into one knot, Mikiko brings her Blazing Wind down on top of it, and the finale crushes and bursts it all at once. Best against a crowd. Its damage grows with both of their Attack levels and ability tiers.
## Bots and team ultimates
- Bots only go for a team ultimate in a big fight: a lot of enemies (6 or more within 16 blocks of you or the bot) or a very strong one (a boss, or something at least 3x as strong as you by Karma Sense). A couple of weak mobs never get one.
- In a fight like that, bot teammates save their own ultimate when their partner is ready, and two bots (Rhalix + Mikiko) do team ultimates together on their own.
- A Rhalix or Mikiko bot asks YOU for one in a fight like that when you're both ready ("Rhalix: Ready for Blazing Judgment!"): press the ultimate key or {key:accept_request} to go, or just let it pass. A bot asks at most every 30 seconds.
## Synergies
Some characters simply fight better together - see Party & Bots > Synergy and bond.

pages.title: Parties
pages.text:
- Parties hold up to 4 (players and bots together, 3 bots each at most). In creative, /xeno partylimit <1-16> changes that for the world.
- Invite: right-click a player with an empty hand, or /xeno party invite <name>. Accept from the request card ({key:accept_request}) or the chat message (answering in chat clears the card too).
- Party members see each other's health and Karma and can't hurt each other (except in a battle you both agreed to).
- The party frames on the left get smaller the bigger the party (4+, 6+ and 9+ members), and split into two columns when they still wouldn't fit.
- The Party menu (main menu > Party) has a slot for everyone the party can hold: empty ones have a "+ Add bot" button. With a bigger limit the rows get smaller, and two columns once they won't fit.
- Ai-oni and Rhalix can never be in the same party.

pages.title: Party HUD
pages.text:
Every HUD style (Blazing Wind, Modern and Classic) shows your party members with their health and Karma bars, each with its numbers (current/max).
- Your own health and Karma bars show their numbers too (Classic: health beside the hearts, Karma over the skill slots).
- With DragonMineZ: each member also gets a ki bar (yellow) with its numbers (current/max) - players and bots alike.
## Live portraits
- The round portraits (yours, and your party members' and bots' when they're in view) make the same face as the character in the world, frame by frame: blinks, expressions, talking (voice chat or a chat line), battle damage, sleeping, knocked out, starving, Demon's Remnants and Lunar eyes, Fox King's hair, outfits, hoods, glasses and goggles, and a DragonMineZ form's hair colour.
- A member who's too far away to be seen shows their drawn portrait instead.

pages.title: Bot teammates
pages.text:
- Add one: main menu > Party > an empty slot > Add bot, or /xeno bot. A bot is one of your other characters, with your saved stats and loadout for them (and your ability levels).
- Click a bot in the Party menu for its options: Mode (Neutral, Aggressive, Mining), Bot menu (its gear, offhand and bag) and Dismiss.
- Bots fight with combos and their skills, drink potions, and walk to healing pods when they're hurt.
- Rhalix and Mikiko bots do team ultimates (Gravity Fox Fire, Blazing Judgment) with each other, and ask you for one when you're both ready - but only against a lot of enemies or a very strong one. Press the ultimate key to join (Combat > Team attacks).
- Party Swap (Party menu): when a bot is lost, another of your characters takes its place.
- Bots keep everything they carry: going down, bleeding out, dismissing, logging out, a Journey, another dimension or you travelling far away. (A bot that's down when you go to another dimension or far away isn't brought along: it goes home to recover for 5 minutes, things and all.) Add them back and their things are all there.
- Even if the game or server crashes: your bots are saved with you at every autosave, so they come back with what they had then (like your own inventory does).

pages.title: Bots off duty
pages.text:
Characters that aren't on your team get on with their own lives while you play (a minute at a time, while you're online):
- Training (Attack and Defense; with DragonMineZ also TP for its own Dragon Ball character), relaxing (after going down a lot lately, or after a long time with you), out at a party (two or three of them together), their own DMZ missions (with DragonMineZ: TP), mining (ore into their own bag - rarer ores the higher your Mining level, never once the bag and extra tabs are full; it adds to your Mining level), chopping wood, building (Building XP).
- The bot pick screen (/xeno bot) shows what each is up to, with a little animated badge.
- Busy ones can't join - unless your bond with them is 60+: then they drop it and come. They bring what they got (it's in their bag) and their new levels.
- With a bond of 50+, right-click a card to give them a job (mining, wood, training, DMZ missions, building, relax) - they keep at it until you call them back (or add them).
- A teammate you have a bond under 30 with may wander off to train after 20 quiet minutes (never in a fight, a Journey, the Tower or VR).
- Season-locked characters do nothing until unlocked. In creative, /xeno offduty off (or on) turns it all off or on for the world.

pages.title: Bots' extra bag
pages.text:
Every bot teammate has three extra tabs of 54 slots each (six rows, like a double chest) on top of its normal bag, just for being a bot. Bots from before keep everything: their old tabs move over tab for tab, slot for slot.
- Open them from its Bot menu: the tabs Bag / Extra 1 / Extra 2 / Extra 3 above its things. Shift-click puts things into the tab you're looking at.
- Bots use everything in all four tabs: crafting materials, food, potions, torches, ammo, Blasters and gear upgrades. What they pick up or mine goes into the extra tabs once the bag is full; a bot only says its inventory is full when every tab is full.
- The extra tabs only exist while that character is a bot. When you play the character yourself you have its normal inventory; the extra tabs wait (kept in your save) and are back, exactly as they were, the next time it's a bot.
- They stay with the bot through everything its bag does: logging out, a crash, dismissing and adding it again, going down and going home, a Journey, the Hekublade.
## Keeping tidy
- A bot keeps its things tidy by itself: a few seconds after it picks something up or crafts, and now and then when it's idle. It merges part stacks, keeps its best weapon, ranged weapon, ammo, shield, totems, some food, torches and potions in its bag, and sorts the rest into the extra tabs: blocks, then ores and materials, food, gear, then everything else.
- It never throws anything away and never touches what it's wearing or holding. It waits while you have its inventory open - press Sort there to tidy right away.
- Journey teammates have no extra tabs (what they find comes to you).

pages.title: Bots transforming
pages.text:
Bots have their characters' transformations too: a Mikiko bot can go Fox King (lasting as long as yours, with your mastery) and a Rhalix bot can call up Demon's Remnants. It costs the bot its own Karma.
- On their own they rarely do it - now and then in a hard fight, more often when badly hurt.
- When you transform (Fox King, Demon's Remnants, Netsu, the Lunar form, a fully charged weapon summon - or a DragonMineZ form), the bots near you follow your lead: within a few seconds, one after another, each goes into its form if it can afford it and there's a fight on or close by.
- With DragonMineZ they also go into their best Dragon Ball form (see Bots: ki, full power and forms).

pages.title: Bots: torches, guns and healing
pages.text:
## Torches
- A bot teammate with torches in its bag lights up dark places as you explore (caves and the like): a torch on a wall or the floor wherever it's darker than light level 7, so they end up spaced out. Never in the Tower, Journey, VR or rooms.
## Guns
- Bots never run out of ammo, but they reload when the magazine is empty (as long as that gun takes to reload) and fire in short bursts at a capped rate - no endless stream of bullets.
- With DragonMineZ they use the Blaster Rifle, Burst Cannon and Blaster Mortar too, if they have one in hand or in their bag: the Rifle in quick volleys (up to 28 blocks), the Burst Cannon three blasts every 1.8 s, the Mortar one huge blast every 5 s (24 blocks, never up close).
- Blaster durability is their ammo, the same as yours: one use a shot (a burst for the Burst Cannon), and the gun breaks when it runs out.
- They hold fire while you or a teammate is in the line of fire (the Mortar also while one is near the target). Their kills count as yours, like other bot kills.
## Kaeru's Fox Heal
- Kaeru as a bot uses Fox Heal on party members near her (8 blocks) who are under half health or downed - you, other players in your party, or your other bots.
- It costs her Karma and has its normal cooldown (shared with Fox Heal in her loadout).
- Playing as Kaeru, your own Fox Heal brings a downed bot teammate within 8 blocks straight back up too, the same as a downed player (a downed player comes first).

pages.title: Bots on their own
pages.text:
When things are quiet (no fight, no enemies close, nobody hurt), bots look after themselves:
## Furnaces
- A bot with raw ore or raw food puts it in a free furnace within about 10 blocks (a smoker for food, a blast furnace for ore), with fuel from its bag, and collects the result later.
- It never touches a furnace that already has something cooking or waiting to be taken out.
## Sharing
- A spare weapon goes to another of your bots that would fight better with it, or a sword to one of your foxes (they hold it in their mouth) if it's stronger than theirs.
- They also hand each other a spare shield, food for a hurt teammate with none, and the one item a teammate is short of for a craft.
## Crafting
- Bots don't ask to craft or repair - when it's safe and their bag has room, they just make the better gear (or fix worn gear, under 25% durability, at most once every 15 minutes per item) and tell you what they made.
- If a bot is one item short, it only asks you for it when you actually have that item on you ([Give 1 & craft] / [No thanks]). If you don't, it doesn't bother you: it mines the ore itself when it can, or drops the idea.
- No crafting table about? They make their own from planks or a log. They don't craft with a full bag.
- One to three ores short of an upgrade, with the right pickaxe, they mine the ore nearby themselves (never in a fight, never far from you).
## Shields
- Bots wear their best shield and raise it against arrows, drawn bows, creepers about to blow and enemies swinging at them.
## Characters
- Flying bots range up to 32 blocks from you, but come straight back if you're attacked.
- Ultima absorbs Data Shards when his Data runs low or he's badly hurt, mends your robots and (with DragonMineZ) rewrites wild ones.
- Yuri looks about now and then for hamburger makings: she picks up what's lying near, and tells you where wheat or cows are.
- Bots in a vehicle with you shoot from their seats with a bow, crossbow or gun.

pages.title: Pets and the Pet Whistle
pages.text:
Your pets belong to you, not to one character: Mikiko's foxes and Rhalix's winged companions stay with you whoever you play.
- The Pet Whistle calls all of them to you at once - foxes and winged companions - for any character. A fox riding on your back hops down.
- It also brings back pets that ran away from a fight, once they've calmed down (the Pets menu shows how long).
- The Pets menu's 'Whistle everyone back' button and /xeno fox call do the same.
- Craft: an iron ingot, rabbit hide and string (or iron nuggets around a feather, with string). Old Fox Whistles are Pet Whistles now.

pages.title: Going down and reviving
pages.text:
- With a party or bot teammates, you go down instead of dying (unless you carry a Totem of Undying in your hand - or anywhere in your inventory with the Inventory Totem mod - which is used up as usual). A red circle appears around you.
- A teammate (player or bot) standing in the circle for 2 seconds revives you; the ring fills with green. Bots get downed and revived the same way.
- When you're revived you get 10 seconds of invincibility and a shockwave that stuns the enemies nearby.
- If nobody is left who could come for you, you bleed out after 10 seconds. /xeno giveup respawns you straight away.
## Revive warp
- Lock on ({key:lock_on}) to a teammate who's down (a player in your party or a bot) - the lock-on turns green and shows REVIVE.
- Hold right-click for 1 second (empty hand or holding anything: while you're locked on to someone who's down, right-click doesn't use your item) to teleport right next to them, into their circle. It costs 30 Karma; you need to be within 48 blocks. It doesn't work in VR or in a battle.
- As Rhalix you arrive casting a Karma shield: a purple dome around you both that stops enemy arrows and other projectiles, throws back enemies who come at it and keeps hits from outside off you. It lasts while you revive them (up to 15 seconds) and drops once they're up or you step out.
- The Rhalix bot does this on its own when a teammate goes down more than 8 blocks away and it has 30 Karma.

pages.title: Synergy and bond
pages.text:
Certain characters in the same party and within 24 blocks get a synergy (bots count, so you can try it solo): Partners (Rhalix + Mikiko), Skyland Bond (Rhalix + Sky Patrol / Kyrie), Goofy Rivals (Mikiko + Ultima), Soul Link (Mikiko + Kaeru), Brothers (Stevie + Garry), Tenjo Siblings (Yuri + Ultima), Old Friends (Zane + Mikiko), Married (Max + Technica).
## Bond
- Every teammate character has a bond level with yours, 0 to 100. It grows a little just by being together, much faster fighting side by side, with every kill one of you makes, and a lot with every revive.
- Higher bond = stronger synergy (double at bond 100), and a synergy's downside fades out - Soul Link's shared death is gone at bond 50.
- Every 10 levels of your best bond with someone in your party: +5 max hearts (+300 with DragonMineZ).
- Bots share it: each bot has its own bond with its teammates (its character's, the one you'll have when you play it) and gets the same bonus hearts from its best bond, on top of its level health. Bots get their synergies too (damage, Soul Link's lighter hits, faster Karma, Old Friends' cheaper skills).
## Bots are treated like players
A bot uses its own character's stats, all kept in your save for that character: Character Level hearts, Attack and Defense levels, ability tiers and levels (its skill uses level them up), Appetite (food heals it more), Building (the torches and Dragon Balls it places), gun level, fall damage and DragonMineZ stats. What it earns is waiting for you when you play that character.
- The Party menu shows your bond with everyone, the active synergies, and [S] opens the Team Synergy panel.

pages.title: Mikiko
pages.text:
The Fox King, fire and wind.
- Hekublade: summon / put away with {key:summon_blade}. Nobody else can keep it. Upgrade its edge at a Karma Altar with Sky Crystals or Corrupted Shards.
- Everything he defeats with it is sealed inside. Step into the Hekublade realm with {key:hekublade_realm} (blade in hand) to walk among the sealed souls - right-click one to free it.
- Aerial blade combo: launch, juggle, and spike them into the ground.
- Fox King mode ({key:fox_king}): +50% max Karma, faster and stronger. The more he masters it, the longer it lasts - see Mikiko: Fox King mastery.
- His fire cooks the raw food he carries. At Character Level 50 he can fly on the wind (double-tap jump).
- He tames foxes with rabbit meat (2 at most). They're yours whoever you play: the Pet Whistle calls them back.
- He's wanted by Aurora's Government: hide your face (a hood or helmet) at Gov terminals.

pages.title: Mikiko: Fox King mastery
pages.text:
Like a DragonMineZ form, Fox King mode ({key:fox_king}) has a mastery from 0 to 100. The more Mikiko uses it, the longer it lasts.
## Gaining mastery
- +0.05 for every second he spends in the form.
- +0.1 for every hit he lands in it (at most one every half second).
- +0.5 for every kill in it.
## What it does
- Length: 90 seconds at mastery 0, 180 at 50, 270 (three times as long) at 100.
- Mastery 25: transforming costs 20 Karma instead of 30.
- Mastery 50: it recovers in 90 seconds instead of 120.
- Mastery 75: it costs only 10 Karma and recovers in 60 seconds.
- Mastery 100 (MAX): +45% attack in the form instead of +35%.
## Where to see it
- Character Customization > Stats: the Fox King row shows your mastery (the red bar fills to 100) and how long the form lasts right now.
- While you're in the form, a FOX KING timer above the hotbar counts down how long is left, with your mastery under it.
- A chat message tells you every 10 mastery and at each milestone. Mastery is saved with your character.

pages.title: Mikiko's weapon forms
pages.text:
Mikiko can turn his Hekublade into other things as it levels up.
- Tap {key:summon_blade}: the Hekublade (or whatever form is out) in / away.
- Hold {key:summon_blade}: a wheel of forms opens while power gathers. Point at one and let go to summon it. Held for the full 2 seconds it's the powered-up summon (+damage for 30 seconds), like the old hold-summon. Let go in the middle to cancel. (With only the Hekublade unlocked, holding works as before.)
## What unlocks when
- Shovel: Hekublade level 20 + Mining level 10
- Hoe: Hekublade level 50
- Guns (pistol, rifle, shotgun): Hekublade level 50 + gun level 50
- Axe: Hekublade level 60 + Mining level 30
- Pickaxe: Hekublade level 80 + Mining level 50
- Heku-umbrella: Hekublade level 300
## The Heku-umbrella
- Held up over his head, it keeps the rain off. Rain puts out Netsu three times as fast - not under the umbrella.
- Fall with it out to glide: slow, drifting forward, no fall damage.
Like the blade, forms can't be dropped or stored, and summoning one sends the others away. See 'Summoned guns and tools'.

pages.title: Rhalix's wires
pages.text:
Once Season 2 is unlocked Rhalix fights with his wires too. They have their own level (shown in the stats screen), raised by using them.
- Tap {key:summon_blade}: wires out / away. Hold it: the wheel of what to make out of them (same as Mikiko's: let go on one, a full charge powers it up).
## The wires
- Attack: he swings them round - everything in front of him up to 4 blocks away gets hit. He winds the wires up over his shoulder and cracks them across in one lash (three grayish-white strands, sparking at the tip). Out, they hang loose from under his sleeve - no handle.
- Lock on ({key:lock_on}) and hold use: the wires bind the target and turn red. They can't move, and their Karma drains (their Ki with DragonMineZ; a mob loses a little health). Up to 8 seconds, then 20 seconds before the next bind.
- A player caught in a bind can mash attack to break free.
## What else he can make
- Wire Sword: any time.
- Guns: wires level 50 + gun level 50.
- Shovel: wires 20 + Mining 10. Hoe: wires 50. Axe: wires 60 + Mining 30. Pickaxe: wires 80 + Mining 50.

pages.title: Summoned guns and tools
pages.text:
The guns and tools Mikiko and Rhalix make from their weapons (no other mods needed).
## Guns
They handle like TACZ guns (same controls, TACZ not needed):
- Left click fires. Pistol: semi-auto, one shot a click. Rifle: full auto - hold to keep firing - long range, goes through one target. Shotgun: pump action, 7 pellets a shot, short range.
- Hold right click to aim down the sights: the gun comes up to the middle of the screen and you look along its sights (the rifle through its scope), the view zooms in (rifle the most), the mouse turns slower to match, you walk a little slower and can't sprint.
- Aimed shots are far more accurate. From the hip the crosshair shows the spread: it opens up while you move, jump or fire fast, and closes again when you stand still. A hit shows a marker (red for a kill).
- Each shot kicks the view up a little (less when aimed or sneaking).
- With TACZ installed, its own shoot / aim keys and its Hold To Aim and zoom sensitivity settings are used.
- Infinite ammo - but each shot wears the gun. More gun level, more durability (190 shots at gun level 50, 1,540 at 500).
- When one breaks there's a 30-second wait before another gun can be summoned (the wheel shows it).
- Putting a worn gun away doesn't mend it: summoned again it comes back just as worn, unless it rested 30 seconds.
- Hekublade guns can set what they hit on fire; wire guns snag it (a moment of Slowness).
- Hits train your gun level.
## Tools
- Better than diamond (netherite-tier), never break, and dig faster the higher the weapon level.

pages.title: Show weapons
pages.text:
Characters whose weapon is in the mod can summon it, like Mikiko's Hekublade.
- Tap {key:summon_blade}: it appears in your hand with a little glow; tap again to put it away.
- Max: his knife. Sam: her bat. Logan and Keita: their swords. Zane (Season 3): his broom. Garry: his microphone.
- It can't be dropped, stored or hung up, never wears out, and vanishes when you die or switch character. The ones you find or craft are separate, ordinary items.
- Bots of these characters summon theirs in a fight and keep it in hand unless they carry a much stronger weapon (the microphone is no weapon, so Garry's bot doesn't).
- Characters without a weapon item yet (Kyrie, Lexy, Technica, Stevie, Yuri, Kill, Ai-oni, Senju) just don't react to the key.

pages.title: Rhalix
pages.text:
Gravity and wings.
- Wings out / away with {key:toggle_wings}; fly by double-tapping jump - but only so high above the ground.
- Kishi, his gravity, pins enemies; it's half of the Gravity Fox Fire team ultimate with Mikiko.
- With DragonMineZ, Kishi is real DragonMineZ gravity ("Kishi 40G" over the dome): the higher his DragonMineZ level, his Character Level and Kishi's own ability level, the more G (see DragonMineZ > Kishi gravity).
- Character Level 30: Judgment Absorption - a point of crushing gravity at the enemy you aim at or lock onto (or the spot you look at). For 4 seconds it sucks in every enemy within 12 blocks, plus loose items, XP and enemy arrows, squeezes them and collapses. Allies are never pulled. With Mikiko it becomes the Blazing Judgment team ultimate (Combat > Team attacks).
- Demon's Remnants ({key:fox_king}): his eyes glow red and he's stronger, faster and tougher for 90 seconds.
- Season 2: the Lunar form (pass the Lunar trial by meditating under a full moon).
- He tames bats, parrots, chickens and bees as winged companions.
- His spinning back kick and sword whirl spin his whole body round, and his arms stay on his shoulders when he twists into a punch or cut. His kicks keep his hips square, and his long coat stays with his legs.

pages.title: Rhalix: Gravity Magnet
pages.text:
Rhalix's passive: dropped items and XP orbs within 10 blocks drift to him, trailing a faint purple glow.
- Turn it on or off on the Stats tab of his Character Customization menu (on by default; it's saved for you).
- It leaves alone what another player has only just thrown (for 2 seconds), and does nothing in VR.
- A Rhalix bot teammate does it too - things come to the bot.

pages.title: Kaeru
pages.text:
- She can go into Mikiko's Hekublade (sneak + {key:summon_blade} near him) and watch through it; any skill key casts her soul out into the world (half strength, limited range).
- Her KA, Change: become any creature you aim at, or (sneaking) the block you look at, for 60 seconds. Every Change wears on her, and too many burn it out.
- Soul Splitter: split your soul off to fight beside you; your health, damage and Karma are shared between the souls. Each soul gets its share of your stats - half of your health, Attack, Defense and (with DragonMineZ) your Dragon Ball health, melee and ki damage with one soul.

pages.title: Ultima
pages.text:
- Power Output: he starts at 25% and ramps to 45%, 70% and 100% the longer a fight goes (faster with Output Surge). Each step fights differently: dodges, flying blasts, heavy slams, then everything at max. Overload (super slot) goes past 100% - and burns him up.
- He runs on Data, not food: absorb Data Shards (from Data Ore) for Data and a little healing.
- Data Sense ({key:karma_sense}) scans for living things AND ores - but C-souls and Corrupted Ore crash it.
- With DragonMineZ he can tame the Xenoverse Robot with Data Shards.

pages.title: Yuri, Technica and the rest
pages.text:
- Yuri (Season 2): the hacker - everything runs off her holographic laptop (Virus Upload and more). With Ultima: Tenjo Siblings synergy.
- Technica: the inventor - twin Uzis (explosive and gravity rounds), gravity boots, a visor and a wing cloak.
- Max: daggers, the Wind element, Vampire Cut KA. Lexy: freakish strength. Kyrie: rapier, boxing and Gravity. Sam: bat, Clear Space and time bombs.
- Stevie and Garry: the Disco Dojo brothers (Brother Blast hits much harder together).
- Logan, Kill and Keita: the Sky Rebellion. Zane (Season 3): Fire, Ice and Thunder spells from his Magical Orb.
- You: build your own characters (10 slots) with a race and element.

pages.title: Falling, wings and fire
pages.text:
## Fall damage
- Anyone with wings (Rhalix, the Skylanders, a winged You character - not a demon in human form) and Mikiko take no fall damage.
- Everyone else takes 75% less. Party bots too.
## Fire in your hands
- Anyone with the element of fire (a fire You character, anyone given fire, and Mikiko always) can right-click a stick to light it into a torch. Sneak to use the block as normal instead.

pages.title: Mikiko: triple jump and flight
pages.text:
- Mikiko learns wind flight at Character Level 150 (it used to be 50).
- Until then he double jumps. With his Hekublade at level 30 or more, jump a third time in mid-air and the Hekublade appears under his feet: he rides it like Hekublade Scatter's blade-surf (a stronger blade rides longer).
- Once he can fly, the third jump is gone (double-tap jump flies instead).

pages.title: Skylander Wings
pages.text:
- Skylanders drop their wings when killed: one in four, guardians half the time (not wingless ones).
- Only Mikiko eats them: each pair gives +10 levels to every stat - Speed, Attack, Defense, Mining, Crafting and Smelting.
- For anyone else they're a trophy.

pages.title: Hamburgers
pages.text:
- Craft one from bread, cooked beef and something green (kelp, dried kelp, fern, grass or seagrass).
- Yuri cooks them: sneak + right-click holding bread or cooked beef - one bread and one cooked beef make two burgers, no greens needed. Her bot looks for the ingredients too.
- A burger heals 40% of your health and gives Regeneration II for 5 seconds.
- Then a wait before the next: Mikiko 5 seconds, Rhalix 3 seconds, everyone else 10 (the hotbar shows it).

pages.title: Curing the Aurora virus
pages.text:
- Yuri and Technica can cure the Aurora virus for anyone in their party.
- Sneak + right-click an infected party member (a player or a bot) with an empty hand: a quick treatment, the virus is gone and they're immune for 5 minutes.
- Their bots do it by themselves for anyone infected close by.
- 30 seconds between cures.

pages.title: Journey
pages.text:
Main menu > Journey. You and one partner (or alone) pick a party of 8 and walk a floating path: battles, scenario battles, healing pods and a boss at the end.
- Before each battle choose who to bring; when the one you're playing goes down, the next tags in.
- Health carries over and nothing heals you mid-battle: heal and revive at the Heal/Enhance shop with Journey Coins.
- Difficulties Easy, Normal, Hard, Insane, Xeno: beat one to open the next. Clearing pays Money.

pages.title: Tower
pages.text:
Opened from the Collection (the book at the Mountain Village Element School). Arena floors with waves of enemies you haven't finished in your Collection.
- Clear every wave to go up. Kills only save to your Collection at a checkpoint: floor 10, then every 10 floors.
- Every 10 floors: a bigger arena, more Collection credit per kill (x1 on floors 1-9, x2 on 10-19, x3 on 20-29...) and tougher enemies.
- Your party can come. Healing is limited on each floor.
## Tower Level
- Playing the Tower levels up your Tower Level (yours as a player, the same whichever character you play): Tower XP for every kill (your bots' and pets' kills too), every wave, every floor cleared (more the higher the floor) and a big bonus for beating a boss floor.
- Every 10 Tower Levels your kills count double in your Collection, in the Tower or anywhere else: x2 at level 10, x4 at 20, x8 at 30, x16 at 40...
- In the Tower it multiplies with the floor's: Tower Level 20 (x4) on floor 25 (x3) = every kill counts x12.
- It only multiplies Collection kills (and so the Collection's every-100 stat boosts) - not Money, bounties or drops.
- The purple bar under the Tower bar shows your Tower Level, progress and what your kills count right now. It's also in the stats screen (Tower row, and Kill multiplier under Status), and /xeno tower level.

pages.title: Famished
pages.text:
A modifier that makes your hunger bar go down faster (the Hunger effect, all fight long).
- Tower: none below floor 10, then a 3% chance a floor is Famished for every 10 floors climbed, up to 40%. It shows in the Tower bar at the top ("Famished") and in chat.
- Journey: a chance each battle by difficulty - Easy never, Normal 5%, Hard 15%, Insane 25%, Xeno 40%. It shows under the battle info (top left).
- Bring food!

pages.title: VR
pages.text:
Yuri's VR room (a VR console, or /xeno vr): the room reshapes itself into an outdoor place. Free training against VR Ultima, plus challenges with rules (a certain character, a small party, no healing, a time limit) and a reward for the first clear. Nothing in VR is real: no drops, no Collection or bounty kills, and losing just ends the session.
## Rewards
- First clear of a challenge: 12-19 emeralds, 2 data shards, a Karma potion and a big chunk of stat XP.
- Clearing it again: 3-5 emeralds and a little stat XP - but repeat clears pay at most 15 emeralds a day (an in-game day: it resets at dawn, so every 20 minutes or after sleeping through the night). After that you can keep replaying for training (the stat XP still counts), with no more emeralds until the next day. First clears are never limited.
- The VR console shows how many repeat emeralds you have left today and when it resets.

pages.title: The Recarnet
pages.text:
The show's world, a dimension of its own. Hold right-click with a Recarnet Pass to travel there and back.
- Sky islands with Skylanders, Government facilities, Order hideouts, human towns (people, not villagers) and Sky Haters.
- Season 2: Aurora City at its center, inside its wall.

pages.title: Factions
pages.text:
Your standing with the Government, the Sky Rebellion, the Sky Patrol & Skylanders and the Townsfolk, -1000 to 1000, separately for each character.
- It changes Gov terminal and villager prices, whether a group attacks you on sight, and bounty pay.
- Main menu > Factions > click a faction for every way to raise or lower it.
- Government: donate emeralds or data shards and hand back Gov gear at a Gov terminal (sneak + right-click it with them), defend Gov agents, hunt the Sky Rebellion and the Order, clear corruption. Getting caught in a facility or hurting agents makes them hate you.
- Fights in the Tower, VR or a Journey are training: the Gov agents and Sky Rebellion members there don't change your real standing.
## Raids
- When the Government, the Sky Rebellion or the Townsfolk see you as Hostile or Hated, now and then (a roll every 2 in-game minutes: 5% at Hostile, up to 18% at -1000) they send a raid after you, wherever you are in the Overworld or Recarnet. Never in a Journey, the Tower, VR or a Room, and never on Peaceful. The Sky Patrol & Skylanders don't raid.
- You get a warning first (a title, a siren, a raid bar), then 3 waves (4 if they hate you) - bigger the more people are with you.
- Government: helicopters packed with soldiers fly in and drop them on you, and armored trucks and cars full of soldiers drive in. Everyone shoots from their seats - drivers too - then they pile out and fight. A Commander leads the last wave.
- Sky Rebellion: rebels dive out of the sky on their wings; Logan, Kill or Keita leads the last wave.
- Townsfolk: an angry mob marches out from the nearest town - pitchforks, axes, torches - led by a Militia Captain.
- Beat every wave: Raid repelled! +40 standing with them (the screen and chat show what it is now, and if it moved you up a tier), loot for everyone who fought (Money too, for a Government raid), and no raid from them for 3 days. Die, run more than 160 blocks away or leave and they give up (1.5 days before they try again). At most one raid a day.
- Fighting off a raid doesn't lower your standing, and raiders never break blocks. Friends nearby can help; bot teammates fight the raiders.
- Off switches: config raids (all, or each faction), gamerule xwFactionRaids. Operators: /xeno raid gov, sr or town starts one, /xeno raid stop ends it, /xeno raid status shows your odds.

pages.title: Government
pages.text:
- Gov Supply Terminal: Government gear for Money (prices follow your standing). It face-scans you.
- Facilities: break things or open containers with staff around and you're wanted - every guard comes for you.
- Healing pods: stand inside to heal and wash bad effects away. Bots and NPCs use them too.
- Karma Scanner visors: see anyone's Karma Level (next page). Guards wear them too.

pages.title: Karma Scanners
pages.text:
Government visors worn on your head: look at anyone and their Karma Level counts up beside the crosshair. Read someone past your scanner's capacity and it blows apart.
## The tiers
- Karma Scanner: overloads above 50,000, reads 48 blocks out. Gov terminal, 600 Money.
- Advanced Karma Scanner: 5,000,000, 64 blocks. Gov terminal at Friendly standing (6,000), or craft: Karma Scanner + 4 mod chips + 3 data shards + an eye of ender.
- Elite Karma Scanner: 500,000,000, 96 blocks. Gov terminal at Honored (40,000), or craft: Advanced + 4 mod chips + 2 diamonds + 2 amethyst shards.
- Omni Karma Scanner: NO LIMIT - reads any Karma Level and never breaks, 128 blocks. Gov terminal at Revered (250,000), or craft: Elite + 4 Xeno Dragon Scales + a nether star + 2 data shards + a mod chip.
## Colours
- Dye one in a crafting grid like leather armor: the lens and its lights take the colour, the frame shows the tier (grey, white, black and red, gold).
- With the Scanner Eye mod on, a stronger scanner lets it mark enemies further out (Advanced 32, Elite 48, Omni 64 blocks).
## Guards
- Gov guards wear scanners (tougher guards and guards far from spawn get better ones; Commanders an Elite) and scan whoever they fight - you'll see the beam and your reading.
- Too strong for a guard's scanner? It blows apart in their face and they panic and run for a while instead of fighting. Wearing it down with hits does the same.
- In the Tower, Journeys and VR they panic too, run for 3-5 seconds and then vanish (teleport out). A vanished soldier counts as gone for the wave, but it's no kill: no drops, XP or Collection credit. Tower and Journey bosses (Gov Commanders) shrug it off and keep fighting.

pages.title: Bounties, Collection and Money
pages.text:
- Bounty boards (village plazas, or craft one): three bounties a day for emeralds, Money, stat XP and sometimes something rare.
- The Collection counts every enemy type you defeat (bots' and pets' kills count): every 100 of one gives a stat boost.
- Money comes from enemies and bounties, carried as Money notes.

pages.title: Villages rebuild
pages.text:
Villages remember how they looked the first time you came by. If something gets wrecked - a creeper, a ghast, fire, a raid - the townsfolk and villagers who live there put it back, block by block, exactly as it was.
- They work in the daytime, and only when no monsters are around.
- They build from the bottom up, door and bed halves together.
- Only gaps get filled: a different block you put there yourself is left alone.
- What players dig out stays dug: blocks you (or your bots and pets) break, and holes from TNT you lit or your own blasts, are never put back - so you can take a bell, a bookshelf or a wall and it won't come back. Put the same block back yourself and they look after it again.
- Chests come back empty, crops come back as fresh seedlings.
- They won't build within 3 blocks of you (so you can't get walled in).
- Recarnet's towns and the huts townsfolk build for themselves get rebuilt too.
- Turn it off with /gamerule xwVillageRebuild false. Never in the modes' arenas or Government facilities.

pages.title: Gear and gadgets
pages.text:
- Karma Altar: upgrade the Hekublade's edge.
- Vehicles: buy them at a vehicle dealer for emeralds (they can't be parked in the Tower, Journey or VR arenas). Driving, the vehicle turns to face where you look; W/S speed up and brake, A/D steer (in the helicopter: slide sideways). Anyone riding can shoot out with a gun (summoned guns, Blasters, TACZ guns) - shots never hit the vehicle or the people riding in it.
- Room technology: pulls you and the enemies near you into a copy of the area, so the fight can't wreck the real world. It ends when the enemies are gone or you leave (logging out closes it too - you come back where you opened it).
- Phones: right-click to take a call (you can't fight until you hang up). Calling someone, the phone goes to your ear while it rings - right-click to hang up before they answer.
- Karma Hoodie / SR Hoodie: hide your Karma (and from the Sky Rebellion).

pages.title: Aurora Security System
pages.text:
Aurora City is protected: when a battle starts there - you, a party member or a bot teammate hitting an enemy, or an enemy hitting one of you - the Aurora Security System moves the fight into a Room (a copy of the area around you) so the city can't be wrecked.
- The enemies around you come along, and so do your party members and bot teammates nearby.
- In the Room the copied buildings can be smashed - none of it is real.
- Beat the enemies and everyone is sent back to where they were in the city.
- Outside a battle, Aurora City is like anywhere else: you can mine and build as normal.

pages.title: Levels and stats
pages.text:
No skill tree: you get better at what you do.
- Speed (sprinting), Attack (dealing damage), Defense (taking hits). Together they make your Character Level, which gives max hearts and unlocks skills.
- Mining, Crafting, Smelting and Building level up on their own. High Mining turns your bare hands into a pickaxe: see 'Mining and bare hands'.
- Each character has their own levels.

pages.title: Outgrown gear wears out
pages.text:
The stronger you get, the faster weaker gear wears out.
- Using a weapon or tool that's weaker than the best one of its kind you're carrying (a wooden sword with a diamond sword in your inventory, a stone pickaxe with an iron one), it loses durability faster - more the higher your Character Level and the bigger the gap.
- About 4-5 times as fast at level 500 for a wooden sword next to a diamond one; up to 20 times at the highest levels.
- Your best one wears normally.
- Its last three hits (before it breaks) hit harder than your best weapon would - and the hit that breaks it hits twice as hard - so using up old gear is worth it.
- Not for guns, the weapons and tools characters summon, or anything unbreakable.
- Bot teammates too: and in a fight they use up their weakest weapons first, so the old ones break and are gone, then fight with their best.

pages.title: Mining and bare hands
pages.text:
Mining levels up from every block you break (with any tool or none). Blocks you placed yourself a moment ago give no XP.
- Every level makes you dig faster with any tool, and even faster with bare hands.
## Bare hands as a pickaxe
As your Mining level goes up, your bare hands count as a better and better pickaxe - they get the drops, and dig as fast as that pickaxe would:
- Mining Lv 5: Wooden Pickaxe - stone gives cobblestone, coal ore gives coal.
- Lv 15: Stone Pickaxe - iron, copper and lapis ore.
- Lv 40: Iron Pickaxe - gold, redstone, diamond and emerald ore.
- Lv 100: Diamond Pickaxe - obsidian, ancient debris.
- Lv 250: Netherite Pickaxe. After that your hands get an Efficiency bonus: I at Lv 400, up to V at Lv 1,000.
- Lv 1,000: Master - anything any tool tier in your mods can mine (modded ores that need more than netherite).
- Your hands also dig wood and dirt as fast as an axe or shovel of the same tier.
- 'Bare hands' means an empty hand or holding something that isn't a tool or weapon (a block, food, a torch...). Tools work as always.
- Hands have no enchantments: no Silk Touch or Fortune.
- Hover Mining in the stats screen to see what your hands mine like now and the next tier.
- Bots mining with bare hands use your Mining level the same way (it's one level for all your characters). A bot that can't get anything out of an ore (no good enough pickaxe, hands not strong enough yet) leaves it alone.

pages.title: Speed: stepping up blocks
pages.text:
- With your Speed stat above 100 you step straight up a full block without jumping. Above 200 it's two blocks, above 300 three, and so on: one more block every 100 levels.
- Don't want it? Main menu > Settings > Movement: Auto step-up.

pages.title: Ability levels and tiers
pages.text:
Every skill and ultimate levels up the more you use it (per character).
- Level 1 to 10 in each tier: every level takes 3% off its Karma cost and cooldown (-27% at level 10).
- At level 10 an Upgrade button appears on the skill's card in Character Customization > Skills. The next tier hits much harder (x1.3 damage per tier) but costs more Karma and has a longer cooldown, until you level it to 10 again.
- 10 tiers. The tier shows on the skill bar (T2, T3...) and every card shows its tier, level and progress.
- Bots use your levels for their character.

pages.title: Appetite (hunger level)
pages.text:
The more food you eat, the more your Appetite levels up.
- Every level makes food fill you 1% more (+100% at level 100).
- Every 10 levels you can hold another whole layer of hunger bars (20 more food points). The food bar changes colour for each layer, and 'x2/3' shows which layer you're eating from.
- Sprinting, regeneration and starving work like normal: they follow the top layer.

pages.title: Building
pages.text:
The more blocks you place, the more your Building levels up (per character; it doesn't change your Character Level).
- Every 10 levels: +1 block of reach for placing, breaking and using blocks (not for attacks). Up to +8 blocks at level 80.
- Every 20 levels: +0.1% chance a block you place isn't used up (survival only). Up to 50% at level 10,000.
- A normal block gives 1 XP, one that breaks instantly (torches, flowers, seeds) a quarter. Placing on a spot you already placed on in the last minute gives nothing, so placing and breaking one block doesn't level it.
- Bots level their character's Building too, from the torches and Dragon Balls they place.
- Hover Building in the stats screen to see your reach and keep chance.

pages.title: Tower Level
pages.text:
One level for you as a player (not per character) that goes up the more you play the Tower (Modes > Tower).
- Tower XP: 1 per kill in a run (your bots' and pets' kills count for you), 3 per wave, 10 + the floor number for each floor cleared, and 25 + twice the floor for beating a boss floor.
- Level 10 takes 855 XP (2-3 runs to floor 10, or one run to floor 20). Level 20: 3,230 (3-4 runs to floor 20). Level 30: 7,105. Level 40: 12,480.
## Kill multiplier
- Every 10 levels it doubles how much one kill counts in your Collection - everywhere, not just in the Tower: x1 below 10, x2 at 10, x4 at 20, x8 at 30, x16 at 40, and so on.
- In the Tower it multiplies with the floor's multiplier (x6 with Tower Level 10 on floor 25).
- It counts Collection kills only (and the stat boosts every 100 of them). No enemy's Collection goes past 1000.
- See it: stats screen > Tower row and Kill multiplier, the purple bar in the Tower, or /xeno tower level.

pages.title: Stat Boosts
pages.text:
Rare crystals that add levels straight to one stat of the character you're playing: +1, +2, +5, +10 or +100 levels, for every stat - Speed, Attack, Defense, Mining, Crafting, Smelting, Appetite, Building, Guns, and Hekublade (Mikiko) or Wires (Rhalix, Season 2).
- Right-click to use one; sneak + right-click uses the whole stack. A stat can't go past its max - a boost isn't used up if the stat is already maxed.
- Colour shows the tier: green +1, aqua +2, purple +5, gold +10, red (shimmering) +100. The small icon shows the stat.
## Where they drop
- Enemies and bosses you or your bots kill: about 2% for a +1, 1% for a +2, 0.3% for a +5, 0.08% for a +10. Bosses drop them much more often.
- The +100 is the rarest of all and only drops from very strong enemies: bosses (2.5%), or something at least three times as strong as you (1%).
- Digging dirt, grass, mud and other dirt-like blocks with a shovel: a small chance (0.4%) to dig one up - mostly Mining boosts (not from dirt you placed there yourself in the last minute - that gives no Mining XP either).
- Every time a stat levels up: a 2.5% chance of a boost for that same stat (mostly +1 or +2). Levels from a boost don't count, so boosts never chain.
- Your bots' kills drop boosts for you (only you can pick them up), and their level-ups can give you one too.
- Creative mode: they're all in the 'Xeno Warriors: Stat Boosts' tab.
## Bot teammates
- Give a bot a Stat Boost (put it in its bag or hand from its menu) and it uses it on itself, one a second: Attack, Speed, Defense, Building and Appetite go to that character; Mining, Crafting and Smelting are shared by all your characters, so they go up for you too.
- Hekublade, Wires and Guns boosts aren't a bot's to use - it keeps them for you.
- Bots leave Stat Boost drops on the ground for you to pick up.

pages.title: Starving
pages.text:
- With your food bar (nearly) empty your character looks it: sunken eyes, pale, mouth hanging open - on your character and on the HUD portrait. Everyone else sees it too.
- Eat something and the face goes back to normal.

pages.title: Bond
pages.text: Fighting beside the same teammates raises your bond with them (see Party & Bots > Synergy and bond): stronger synergies, no synergy downsides from bond 50, and +5 max hearts per 10 levels of your best party bond - your bots get the same bond hearts from their own best bond.

pages.title: Soul Splitter skills
pages.text:
- Once the Soul Splitter ability reaches level 21 (tier 3), your split-off soul fights with your own skills too - the ones in slots 1-4 of your loadout, never your ultimate or a KA.
- The higher the level, the more often it casts (every 6 seconds at first, down to 2.5).

pages.title: Gun level
pages.text:
Every character has a gun level (shown in the stats screens with TACZ installed, and for Mikiko and Rhalix, who can make guns).
- It goes up by hitting things with guns: TACZ guns, and the guns Mikiko and Rhalix summon from their weapons (XP = damage dealt, more for a kill).
- Without TACZ, bows and crossbows train it too (half XP).
- Each level adds 0.2% gun damage, up to +150%.
- More gun level, more durability for summoned guns. With TACZ: at gun level 500 your magazine never runs dry.
- Technica is the gunsmith: her gun level starts at 100 and her guns hit 25% harder on top.

pages.title: Playing with DragonMineZ
pages.text:
- Every character has their own DragonMineZ character (race, stats, forms, techniques). A new one opens the race picker.
- Xeno Warriors skills hit as hard as your DragonMineZ stats say: energy skills follow your Ki damage, physical ones your Strike.
- Fighting as Mikiko or Rhalix trains your DragonMineZ stats too.
- Your blasts can clash with ki attacks.
- Bots use every ki technique their character knows - nothing has to be bound to a key for them (see Bots learn ki techniques).
- Bond hearts are much bigger: +300 max hearts per 10 bond levels.

pages.title: Kishi gravity
pages.text:
With DragonMineZ, Rhalix's Kishi dome is a DragonMineZ gravity field. Its G shows over the dome ("Kishi 40G") and next to your Karma bar.
## How many G
- G = 10 x gravity level (1-3: press Kishi again to make it heavier) x DragonMineZ level (x1 to x5) x Character Level (x1 to x3) x Kishi's ability level (x1 to x2).
- A new Rhalix makes 10G (30G at gravity level 3). A maxed one makes 900G at gravity level 3.
- A Rhalix bot uses its own DragonMineZ character and Character Level, and your Kishi ability level.
## What it does to enemies inside
- Works like DragonMineZ gravity: what counts is the G minus the target's own gravity resistance (from their DragonMineZ stats - a strong fighter shrugs off a weak Kishi).
- Players: DragonMineZ's own gravity - slower movement and attacks, weaker stats, heavier falls, ki flight slowed (stopped from 75G), ki and stamina cost more. No elytra or creative-style flying.
- Mobs and bots: the same slowdown, weaker hits, heavier jumps and falls; from 75G they can't jump or fly at all and get pinned to the ground.
- Anyone with DragonMineZ stats loses stamina and ki every second inside.
- It still crushes them for damage every second, as before.
- Allies are never weighed down. Without DragonMineZ, Kishi works the normal way.

pages.title: Bots and DragonMineZ
pages.text:
- A bot with no Dragon Ball character gets a random race and class, saved for that character.
- Bots earn TP while they're out with you (3x DragonMineZ's passive TP), plus TP for every kill.
- Bot menu > Dragon Ball: opens DragonMineZ's menu on the bot's character. Spend its points, start its own missions (see Bots' own missions). Yours comes back when you close it (or log out, get hit, or change character).
- Your bots' kills count for your missions' kill objectives.
- A bot is as tough and strong as its Dragon Ball character: its Vitality adds to its max health, its Resistance cuts the hits it takes, its Strength is its punch, and its Ki / Strike damage power its skills - just like a player of that character. Out of a fight it heals at DragonMineZ's regen rate.

pages.title: Bots' own missions
pages.text:
- A mission started from a bot's Dragon Ball menu is the bot's own. When its target is defeated - by the bot, by you, or by anyone in your DragonMineZ party - it counts for the bot. When it's done, the bot completes it and gets the rewards: TP, alignment, skills, techniques and forms go to its Dragon Ball character, items go in its bag.
- Your own mission only counts if you're on the same one (then you both do).
- When you start a mission, each bot with a Dragon Ball character starts one too: the same one if it can, otherwise its own next one (its enemies come like yours). A chat line tells you what each bot started. Bots never start missions any other time.
- Its places count while you're there. Its talk / hand-in steps count when you talk to that person - or the bot walks over and talks to them itself (see Talk-to missions).
- If the mission you start has a giver standing close by (within 48 blocks), each bot walks over and takes its mission from them ("Kaeru took ... from Dende"). If it can't get there within 30 seconds it starts it anyway.
- Its missions are saved with its character: they're still there after you log out or re-add the bot.

pages.title: Bots train for missions
pages.text:
- If a bot's next mission needs a higher DragonMineZ level than it has, and the level is the only thing in the way, it spends its own TP on its stats until it gets there - then starts the mission with you. A chat line says so ("Kaeru trained up to level 8 (spent 1,234 TP)").
- It pays exactly what DragonMineZ charges you for the same points (free attribute points first), within the same caps.
- It also gets ready by itself: every 5 seconds it looks at the next step of the sagas you and it are on, and trains towards that level with the TP it has. It never starts a mission on its own.
- It only spends what that level costs - the rest of its TP stays for you to spend in its Dragon Ball menu. Nothing is spent for a mission that something else blocks (a step not done, alignment, race...).
- Where the points go depends on its class: Warrior and Berserker mostly Strength, Martial Artist Strike Power, Spiritualist Ki Power and Energy, Cleric Energy and Ki Power, Tank Resistance and Vitality, Paladin a bit of everything. Every class keeps Vitality and Resistance up so it survives.
- Not while its Dragon Ball menu is open, and never with your own points.

pages.title: Bots learn ki techniques
pages.text:
## Every technique, no keys
- A bot fights with every ki attack and strike move its Dragon Ball character knows - not just the ones in its slots. You never have to bind anything for it, and its slots stay as you left them in its Dragon Ball menu.
- It picks what fits: strike moves up close, beams and waves from range, explosions only when the enemy is right there, a giant ball or its hardest hitters for strong enemies, cheap ones for small fry - only what it has the ki for, and not the same one twice in a row.
## Its own ki attacks
- With spare TP a bot creates its own ki attack in DragonMineZ's technique creator, at DragonMineZ's price. A chat line says so ("Kaeru created a new ki attack: Kaeru's Ember Cannon").
- The kind follows its class (Spiritualist: beams and giant balls; Martial Artist: discs and lasers; Berserker: explosions...), the colour its character's, and it's as strong as half its spare TP buys.
- At most one every 8 minutes, 6 in all, and never in the middle of a fight.
## From masters
- When a DragonMineZ master (Goku, Roshi, Piccolo, King Kai, Vegeta, Gohan...) is within 40 blocks and things are quiet, a bot with spare TP walks over, talks to them and learns one of their ki or strike techniques - Kamehameha from Goku or Roshi, Masenko from Piccolo, Dragon Fist from Goku... A chat line says so ("Kaeru learned Kamehameha from Goku").
- Same rules as for you: the same TP price, race limits, and the master's alignment rule (good masters won't teach a bad-aligned bot).
- Masters teach skills too: Kaioken from King Kai, Fly from Goku or Frieza, Ki Control, Potential Unlock, Ki Boost, Ki Protection... ("Kaeru learned Kaioken from King Kai (1,000 TP)"). Fly and Kaioken come first; Jump, Sprint, Ki Sense, Instant Transmission and Fusion are left to you.
- It prefers the kind it has fewest of (ki attack, strike move or skill). Off with botsTalkToNpcs=false.
## Skill levels
- Every 2 minutes or so it may buy the next level of a skill it has, as DragonMineZ's skill menu does for you (same price per level, same max): Kaioken first, then Fly, then the rest - with at most half its spare TP. A chat line says so ("Kaeru trained Kaioken to level 2").
## Using its skills
- Fly: a bot that knows Fly flies like the flying characters do - after you when you fly, up to flying enemies, over gaps. Flying costs it ki (less at higher Fly levels); out of ki it floats down and flies again once it has 20% back.
- Kaioken: against a strong enemy, with over 60% health, it goes as high as its Kaioken level allows (x2 at level 1, x3 at 2, x4, x10, x20) - on top of a form only if that form can stack. It hits harder and loses health every second, as DragonMineZ says. Under 35% health, or when the fight's over, it drops it.
- Ki Boost, Ki Protection, Potential Unlock and the like work through its Dragon Ball stats, as they do for you.
## Spare TP
- Only TP above what its next mission's level still costs: training for missions always comes first (see Bots train for missions).
- Not while its Dragon Ball menu is open, and never with your own TP.

pages.title: Talk-to missions
pages.text:
- When all that's left of your mission is talking to someone - a quest NPC or a master - they come to you (for a bot's mission: as soon as that talk is its next step): a copy appears near you, in any world.
- Talk to them as usual to finish it. Then they vanish in a puff of smoke.
- They also leave if the mission is finished or dropped some other way, after 10 minutes, or when you log out. They're never kept in the world.
- Not if the real one is already within 32 blocks.
## Bots talk too
- A bot whose own mission waits on talking to someone (Dende, a master, whoever it's handed in to) walks up to them and talks to them itself: the real one if they're within 48 blocks and it can walk there, otherwise the copy that came to you. A chat line says so ("Kaeru talked to Dende") and the copy leaves.
- Only when things are quiet: never in the middle of a fight, with enemies close, or when you're in trouble. It gives up after 30 seconds if it can't get there and tries again later - you can always talk to them for it.
- Off with botsTalkToNpcs=false in config/xenowarriors-common.toml.

pages.title: Missions in any biome
pages.text:
- DragonMineZ missions don't care which biome you're in. A mission that says "be in the desert" (or the plains, a forest, rocky land...) to start can be started anywhere, and "go to biome X" objectives (like World Explorer) count as reached wherever you are.
- If a mission wants you to defeat something that only lives in other biomes (bandits, Red Ribbon soldiers and robots, Frieza's soldiers...) and you're somewhere they don't spawn, a group of them comes to you; once that group is gone and you still need more, the next one comes.
- The same for your bots' own missions.
- Places stay as they are: a mission at a structure (Kami's Lookout, except the movie missions) still wants you there. Dimensions never mattered (see the other pages).
- Turn it off with missionsIgnoreBiomes = false in config/xenowarriors-common.toml.

pages.title: Movie missions anywhere
pages.text:
- DragonMineZ's movie missions don't need you at Kami's Lookout. The Movies saga's first step (Kami's Lookout Warning) and the side mission Dende's Lookout Vigil count "be at Kami's Lookout" as done wherever you are - start them and play them anywhere, in any world.
- Dende comes to you for the talk (see Talk-to missions), and your bots talk to him themselves.
- Everything else stays: the level each one needs, the saga order, and the steps before it.
- Off with moviesWithoutLookout=false in config/xenowarriors-common.toml.

pages.title: Mission help
pages.text:
- If a mission wants you to beat a story fighter that never turns up by itself, it's summoned near you a few seconds after the objective starts (once per objective).
- A mission that wants you to have items counts your bots' things too (their bag and extra tabs): split them between you and your bots however you like. Like DragonMineZ, it only counts them - nothing is taken from you or your bots.
- A bot's own missions count its things, yours and your other bots'.
- If a mission needs items, every hostile mob you or your bots kill has a 30% chance to drop one, until you have enough.
- Mikiko masters Kaioken 20 times faster than anyone else.

pages.title: Mission Bag
pages.text:
Your party's bag for DragonMineZ mission items, so they don't fill up your inventory or your bots'.
- Anything a mission still needs (yours or a bot teammate's) goes into it: drops from whatever you or your bots kill, and those items when you pick them up. A message shows how many went in.
- 216 slots (4 pages of 54).
- Open it from the main menu > Party > Mission Bag (or /xeno missionbag). You can take things out, but you can't put anything in.
- What's in it counts for your missions just like your inventory does.
- Once a mission has all it needs, more of that item goes into your inventory as usual.

pages.title: TPs from Journey and the Tower
pages.text:
With DragonMineZ, Journey and the Tower give your DragonMineZ character TPs too (on top of their Money and loot).
## Journey
- Halfway along the path: 150 x difficulty x stage TPs (difficulty 1-5, stage 1-3).
- Clearing the stage: 500 x difficulty x stage TPs (up to 7,500 for Xeno Stage 3).
## Tower
- Every boss floor cleared: 20 TPs per floor (floor 10 = 200, floor 40 = 800).
- Every 50th floor is a milestone: triple TPs (floor 50 = 3,000).

pages.title: The Zombie Saiyan
pages.text:
- A rare boss that comes out at night in the Overworld. It also has a spawn egg.
- As you wear it down it goes Super Saiyan, then Super Saiyan 2 (lightning), then Super Saiyan 3 (long hair). It uses combos, dashes, ki blasts and the Kamehameha.
- Beat it as a Super Saiyan 3 and it collapses. Then it gets back up screaming, throws everyone back, and returns fully healed as a Super Saiyan 4.
- It grows with your DragonMineZ power. Beaten as a Super Saiyan 4, it drops: diamonds, emeralds, Senzu Beans, Karma items, and sometimes a piece of Goku armor with every enchantment.

pages.title: The Xeno Dragon
pages.text:
When you beat the Ender Dragon (the first one or a respawned one), its power doesn't fade: once its death is over, it takes shape again as the Xeno Dragon - a dragon warrior with the Ender Dragon's scales, horns and wings - and glides down onto the island. The exit portal, the XP and the egg still come from the Ender Dragon as usual.
- Its moves: dragon breath (a lingering purple cloud - step out of it), ender fireballs, a wing gust that throws everyone back, a dive from the sky (a purple ring shows where it lands), short ender teleports, and claw combos with a tail sweep. It rears its head before breathing and spreads its wings before a gust.
- It goes Super Saiyan at 75% health, Super Saiyan 2 at 50% and Super Saiyan 3 at 25%. Beaten as a Super Saiyan 3, it becomes a Super Saiyan God, fully healed. Every form makes it a lot faster, and its attacks come quicker.
- As Super Saiyan 2 and as a god it raises two End Crystals that heal it: break them.
## Ultra Instinct
- Beat it as a Super Saiyan God and it falls - then gets back up in Ultra Instinct (Mastered): silver, even faster, dodging some of your hits.
- Now it throws the Dragon Bomb: it holds a huge sphere over its head for 5 seconds, then throws it where you stood. Hit it hard while it charges to make the bomb collapse, or get out of the ring on the ground.
- Only beaten in Ultra Instinct does it drop its loot: Xeno Dragon Scales, a dragon head, dragon's breath, maybe an elytra, diamonds, netherite, a totem, Senzu Beans and other DragonMineZ items, Karma items, a Stat Boost +10 (sometimes a +100), maybe a fully enchanted Goku armor piece - and lots of XP. It counts as a DragonMineZ kill for you or your bot.
- It grows with your party's DragonMineZ power and size. Only one at a time. Off with xenoDragon=false in config/xenowarriors-common.toml.

pages.title: Fusing with a bot
pages.text:
Bot menu > Fuse: you and the bot become one fighter, the DragonMineZ way.
- Potara: the bot needs Potara earrings (any color) in its bag. The stronger fusion.
- Fusion Dance: the bot's Dragon Ball character knows the Fusion Dance skill.
- You take on the fused look and name, and DragonMineZ's fusion bonus: the bot's stats are added to yours (more for Potara, and more the closer your strengths are).
- It lasts DragonMineZ's fusion time (its config). The bot steps out of the world while you're fused and comes back, with all its things, when it ends.
- A Potara fusion that runs its full time breaks the earrings. If you're knocked out, log out, switch characters or change game mode first, the fusion ends early and the earrings go back in the bot's bag.
- While you're fused, other bots' Dragon Ball menus stay closed, and the bot you're fused with still counts as on your team.
- Afterwards there's DragonMineZ's fusion cooldown before you can fuse again.
- The stats work exactly like a DragonMineZ fusion between two players, with the bot's own Dragon Ball character as your partner: each boosted stat of the bot's x 1.75-2.5 (Potara) or x 1.25-2.0 (Fusion Dance), more the closer your two totals are.

pages.title: Bot and mission news
pages.text:
With DragonMineZ, news about your bots and missions - a bot trained up, learned or created a ki attack, took, started or finished a mission, talked to someone, a mission's target or an NPC came to you - shows as small see-through cards on the left of the screen (above the usual pop-ups) instead of filling the chat.
- Want it in chat as before? M menu > Settings > DRAGONMINEZ > Bot / mission news: In chat.
- Things you need to act on stay in chat: the dragon waiting for your wish, fusion started / ended, and why something was refused.

pages.title: Mikiko's Shiyoken fox aura
pages.text:
Mikiko whose Dragon Ball race is Human gets a fox aura in DragonMineZ's Shiyoken forms.
- Shiyoken: a blazing orange-red fire aura, flame fox spirits running in circles round him, embers, and fire lines glowing over his outfit.
- Shin Shiyoken (and Chou Shiyoken, bigger): more and bigger fire foxes, a huge flame fox head rising behind him, black orbs with glowing rims, flame ribbons and brighter lines all over his outfit.
- Everyone nearby sees it. Works with Epic Fight and shader packs.

pages.title: Bots and the Dragon Balls
pages.text:
Give a bot all seven Dragon Balls of a set (put them in its bag) where that set works: Earth's on the Overworld, Namek's on Namek.
- When there's no fight going on, it finds a flat, open spot near you and puts them down in a ring, one-star to seven-star, in order.
- Then it calls the dragon for you. The dragon is yours: the wish menu opens for you and you pick the wish.
- It needs a flat 5x5 spot with room above it; if there's none it tells you and tries again later.

pages.title: Blaster guns
pages.text:
Ki guns in the style of the Blaster Cannon, firing DragonMineZ ki blasts.
- Blaster Rifle: hold right-click for rapid fire (small blasts). Craft: 2 Gete Ingots + a Ki Battery in the top row, an Iron Ingot below the battery.
- Burst Cannon: three quick blasts per shot. Craft: 2 Ki Batteries, 3 Gete Ingots, a Block of Redstone and an Iron Ingot.
- Blaster Mortar: one huge, slow blast with a long reload. Craft: a Blaster Cannon surrounded by Gete Ingots, a Ki Battery on top and an Iron Ingot below.
- Some of DragonMineZ's soldiers carry them, and armed Skylanders too. Mobs holding one shoot it, and sometimes drop it when you beat them.
- Give one to a bot teammate and it shoots it too (see Bots: torches, guns and healing).

pages.title: Skylanders in other worlds
pages.text:
Skylanders turn up on Namek (most often), in the Otherworld and on the Sacred World of the Kai.
- They carry Blaster guns and shoot them at what they fight.
- They're still Skylanders: friendly unless the Sky faction hates you, and they fight the monsters there.
- Beat one and it may drop its gun.

pages.title: Bots: ki, full power and forms
pages.text:
- A bot's ki techniques cost ki from its own Dragon Ball character. Out of ki, it can't use them.
- Low on ki and somewhere safe, it stops and charges (aura and all) until it's full.
- When a fight starts it powers up to 100% release, and against a strong enemy (a boss, a story fighter, anything tougher than it) it transforms into the best form its character has unlocked.
- Forms drain its ki. Once the fight is over it reverts and powers back down to 50%.
- Full power and forms make its hits stronger too, following its Dragon Ball stats.
- When you transform (any DragonMineZ form, or a Xeno Warriors one), your bots follow your lead: a moment later each one goes into its best form if it has the ki and there's a fight on or close by - no strong enemy needed - and it stays in it while you stay in yours.
- Out of a fight their power release follows yours (never under 50%).

pages.title: Screen and sensing
pages.text:
- With the Blazing Wind HUD on, DragonMineZ's own health/ki/stamina bars are hidden: the HUD shows your Ki, stamina, form and power release instead.
- DragonMineZ's technique bar, mission tracker and other panels are moved so they don't sit on top of the HUD.
- Sensing (Karma Sensing or Ki Sense) no longer turns the screen black and white: you still see the auras, outlines and readings, in full color.
